A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same multi-turn jailbreak research, renamed from RL-MTJail to TROJail. The complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D support comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original attacker evaluations, transfer experiments, reward ablations, and judge-agreement measurements in Section 6 and Appendix A.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments in Section 5 and Appendix A and reports additional preliminary-analysis results in Section 3.2.

M1.justification: The reported process-advantage estimator changes: v1 Eq. (8) discounts future rewards, while v2 Eqs. (8)–(9) use an undiscounted sum and explicitly pool normalization across trajectories and turns. The core framework and two rewards remain. Entropy regularization remains documented in Appendix A despite disappearing from the main objective. The PDFs do not establish whether training was rerun.

E1.justification: Both versions train on AdvBench and evaluate on HarmBench, StrongREJECT, and JailbreakBench against the same four victim models. V2 identifies data sources for existing preliminary analyses without establishing expanded dataset, task, or domain coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the main benchmark, difficulty, diversity, ablation, and judge-reliability comparisons. Qwen3Guard receives a new citation but already participates in v1 Table 4.

E3.justification: Figure 3 changes its reported measure from AHS described as computed over interactions to average final outcome reward and adds an unmodified-trajectory control. Figure 4 additionally measures harmfulness across turns. Main benchmark splits, ASR@3 reporting, and stated training budgets remain unchanged; newly disclosed preliminary-study settings do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: V2 strengthens the existing prompt-insertion analysis with an unmodified-trajectory control and adds a comparison of per-turn harmfulness with semantic relevance in Figure 4. Reward ablations, transferability, turn-limit and difficulty analyses remain. The diversity analysis moves to Appendix A rather than being newly added.

E5.justification: Neither version reports random seeds, independent-training-run variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests. V2 introduces no new uncertainty-reporting practice; the three-attempt ASR evaluation rule is retained.

E6.justification: Figure 3 reports different bars under its revised outcome-reward measure and adds the original-trajectory reference. Figure 4 adds harmfulness trajectories and omits v1's one-turn similarity point. Tables 1, 3, and 4 and existing Table 2 transfer scores are unchanged, including the 86.23 average ASR. Table 2's added in-domain scores reproduce existing results.

T1.justification: V2 replaces v1's ambiguously indexed process-reward normalization with the explicitly defined set D_h over all trajectories and turns, and removes discounting from the mathematical estimator. These are limited revisions to formal definitions. No theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: trajectory-level reinforcement learning, two heuristic process rewards addressing sparse supervision, and improved attack effectiveness with generalization. Renaming and revised emphasis do not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: V2 adds an explanation of why semantic relevance supplies more useful intermediate feedback than harmfulness and why longer trajectories have lower final similarity. Its limitations discussion drops v1's causal-sufficiency and nonstationarity caveats, emphasizes potential defensive uses, and clarifies that entropy regularization does not explicitly optimize strategy diversity.

D1.justification: V2 adds Algorithm 1 and specifies preliminary-study trajectory sources, disjoint sampling, the fixed intervention victim, and semantic-analysis datasets and models. Appendix A formalizes diversity aggregation. These mainly expand documentation of existing experiments. The code-access pointer changes from RL-MTJail to TROJail; availability cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: V2 adds references to Perez et al. on LLM red teaming, Li et al.'s SPEED paper, and the Qwen3Guard technical report. The established positioning against single-turn and turn-level optimization remains. Changed author labels for existing model reports are bibliographic edits.

P1.justification: V2 extensively rewrites and reorganizes the narrative: background and empirical patterns become Section 3, the RL formulation moves into Method, results receive a more structured discussion, and diversity moves to Appendix A. The title, method and reward names, terminology, author block, and limitations text also change.

P2.justification: V2 substantially redesigns Figures 1–2, revises Figure 3's axes and control display, and expands Figure 4 into two panels. Table 2 gains shaded in-domain cells and separate ID/OOD averages. Figure 7 moves to the appendix, Algorithm 1 is added, and one example figure is shortened.

improvement.justification: V2 makes the method and empirical motivation easier to assess through clearer organization, explicit normalization and pseudocode, added study details, and the control and signal comparison in Figures 3–4. These provide a limited net improvement with unchanged benchmark evidence. Some gains are offset by Eq. (11) omitting the entropy term still reported in Appendix A and by removal of substantive limitations.
